speaker: Unknown
en: In a AI digital age, energy capacity equals economic capacity.
zh: 在 AI 数字时代，能源容量等于经济容量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why build a new data center and buy a million GPUs if I can't power that?
zh: 如果我没法供电，为什么要建新的数据中心、买一百万块 GPU 呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to see more and more defaults happening on many of those data center projects because the energy won't be there.
zh: 你会看到越来越多的数据中心项目发生违约，因为能源不会到位。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whenever you have the technology to make something easy, that means the bottleneck moves somewhere else.
zh: 每当你拥有让某件事变容易的技术，那就意味着瓶颈转移到了别的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing's a chip anymore, it's a rack.
zh: 现在已经没有什么东西是一块芯片了，而是一个机架。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took me three months to design it, but it's nine months until I can actually start to use it.
zh: 我花了三个月设计它，但还要九个月才能真正开始使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly how many major new memories have you had over the last 30 years?
zh: 过去 30 年里你到底见过多少次重大的新内存？

speaker: Unknown
en: Memory innovation for the first time in 30 years is nigh upon us.
zh: 30 年来第一次，内存创新近在眼前。

speaker: Unknown
en: I declared the death of copper about 25 years ago.
zh: 我在大约 25 年前就宣布了铜的死亡。

speaker: Unknown
en: Eventually I'll be right for all of us hardware guys.
zh: 最终我们这些搞硬件的人都会等到我说对的那一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is like renaissance in front of AI inference accelerator chips and I'm sure I don't even know them all.
zh: 这就像 AI 推理加速器芯片面前的文艺复兴，我敢肯定我甚至都没把它们全认全。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why are you guys funding so many of those anyways?
zh: 你们到底为什么要投这么多这样的公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: You funded your first share too.
zh: 你们当年也投了自己的第一份。

speaker: Unknown
en: Historically, there have not been a hundred competing processor vendors in any industry ever.
zh: 从历史上看，任何行业从来都没有过一百家相互竞争的处理器厂商。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a temporary thing.
zh: 这是暂时的现象。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll convert back to a view.
zh: 它会回归成少数几家。

speaker: Unknown
en: I see it as AI is making it faster to design ships, but actually building them, powering them, and connecting them may be getting harder.
zh: 我把它看作 AI 正在让设计芯片变得更快，但真正制造它们、给它们供电、把它们连接起来可能正变得更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this episode, A16Z's Ragu Ragu Ram and Guido Abedzeller sit down with Pat Gelsinger, general partner at Playground Global and former CEO of Intel and VMware, to discuss the next bottlenecks in AI infrastructure.
zh: 在本集中，A16Z 的 Ragu Ragu Ram 和 Guido Abedzeller 与 Playground Global 普通合伙人、Intel 和 VMware 前 CEO Pat Gelsinger 坐下来，讨论 AI 基础设施的下一个瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pat takes us back to his early days designing Intel's processors, when engineers were inventing the tools they needed to build the chips themselves.
zh: Pat 带我们回到他早期设计 Intel 处理器的日子，当时工程师们在发明他们自己造芯片所需的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: He explains why AI could bring a similar shift today, even as manufacturing timelines, memory bandwidth and power become harder constraints.
zh: 他解释了为什么 AI 今天可能带来类似的转变，即便制造周期、内存带宽和电力正成为更难的约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: They also debate whether the explosion of specialized AI chips will last, why Pat believes memory innovation is finally approaching a breakthrough, and how optical networking could change the architecture of AI clusters.
zh: 他们还辩论了专用 AI 芯片的爆发是否会持续、为什么 Pat 相信内存创新终于接近突破、以及光网络可能如何改变 AI 集群的架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: In drawing on their shared history at VMware, they close with a question.
zh: 借助他们在 VMware 的共同历史，他们以一个问题作结。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would it look like to rebuild virtualization for a world where AI agents, rather than humans, are the primary users?
zh: 在一个 AI 智能体而非人类是主要用户的世界里，为这样的世界重建虚拟化会是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm here with our esteemed guest and dear friend and former boss, Mr. Pat Gelsinger.
zh: 我和我们的尊贵嘉宾、亲爱的朋友、也是我以前的老板 Pat Gelsinger 先生在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome, Pat.
zh: 欢迎，Pat。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pat is currently the general partner at Playground Global.
zh: Pat 目前是 Playground Global 的普通合伙人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as you are very, very well known in the industry for leading.
zh: 但正如你在这个行业里非常非常广为人知的领导经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: Intel, for being the CTO of Intel, of course, leading VMware and many other things.
zh: Intel,担任过 Intel 的 CTO,当然，还有领导 VMware 以及许多其他事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So welcome.
zh: 所以欢迎。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, thank you, Raygu.
zh: 嘿，谢谢你，Raygu。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great to be with you and Guido.
zh: 很高兴和你还有 Guido 在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to me, this feels just a little bit like old home, right?
zh: 而对我来说，这感觉有点像回到老家，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: We superimposed a year of change, right?
zh: 我们叠加了一年的变化，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But you both went the same.
zh: 但你们俩都一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel energetic.
zh: 我感觉精力充沛。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's dive in.
zh: 那我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: There has never been a day when you stopped being energetic.
zh: 你从来没有一天是不精力充沛的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's no news there.
zh: 所以这没什么新闻。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, no, let's start actually from your Intel career.
zh: 不过对，我们就从你的 Intel 职业生涯说起吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Recently, Andreessen Horowitz created this Horowitz Andreessen Academy, which was to find talented people between 16 and 22, and then put them into a modern educational setting so they'd be well prepared for either doing things of their own or joining the companies of today.
zh: 最近，Andreessen Horowitz 创办了这个 Horowitz Andreessen Academy,旨在发掘 16 到 22 岁之间的人才，然后把他们放到一个现代的教育环境中，让他们为either自己做事还是加入当今的公司做好充分准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had a similar experience, like you went to a regular trade school and then jumped into Intel when you were, what, 18 or 19, I should say?
zh: 你有过类似的经历，比如你上了一所普通的职业学校，然后在 18 还是 19 岁的时候跳进了 Intel,我该怎么说？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it was really a sort of magical period.
zh: 是的，那真是一段magic般的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm 16 years old, I accidentally win a scholarship, I go to tech school, I skipped my last year and a half of high school, and Intel comes recruiting when I'm 18 years old.
zh: 我 16 岁，意外地赢得了一份奖学金，我去了技术学校，我跳过了高中最后一年半，然后 Intel 在我 18 岁的时候来招聘。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'd never been on an airplane, had already fallen in love with computers at tech school, and the interviewer, right, Ron Smith was his name, he writes on his page, and I was number 12 that he interviewed that day, and if you've interviewed 12 people in a row, you can't tell male from female by the end of it, right?
zh: 而且我从来没坐过飞机，已经在技术学校爱上了计算机，那个面试官，对，他叫 Ron Smith,他在他的本子上写，我是他那天面试的第 12 个人，如果你连续面试了 12 个人，到最后你根本分不清男女，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm number 12, he says, smart, aggressive, arrogant, he'll fit right in.
zh: 我是第 12 个，他写道，聪明、有冲劲、傲慢，他会很快融入。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I got invited to come to Intel and it just became really glorious.
zh: 所以我被邀请去 Intel,而这一切变得无比辉煌。

speaker: Unknown
en: Starting as a technician, moved into the design team at the end of the 286, engineer number four on the 386, architect and design manager for the 486, all of that while doing my bachelor's, my master's and PhD work.
zh: 从一名技术员做起，在 286 的末期进入设计团队，是 386 的第四号工程师，486 的架构师和设计经理，这一切都是在读我的本科、硕士和博士期间完成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was like the best career that you could possibly have.
zh: 所以这就像你能拥有的最好的职业生涯。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're learning by day and you're putting it to practice at night.
zh: 你白天在学,晚上就在实践。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're creating new, completely new pair of chips.
zh: 你在做全新的、完全崭新的芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: I bet most of what you learned and what you built, there was a big gap because you're breaking new ground.
zh: 我敢说你学到的和你造出来的东西之间有很大的差距,因为你在开辟新领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, in a lot of ways.
zh: 是的,在很多方面都是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it really was a pretty incredible time in the industry.
zh: 那确实是业界一段相当了不起的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember one of the professor classes, he postulated a new Cary Lookahead Adder design, right?
zh: 我记得有一位教授的课,他提出了一个新的 Cary Lookahead Adder(进位先行加法器)设计,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: In one of my classes at Stanford.
zh: 那是在斯坦福我上的一门课里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I said, well, I'm working on the 386 Cary Lookahead Adder, so let me go try it.
zh: 所以我说,好吧,我正在做 386 的 Cary Lookahead Adder,让我去试一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I come back two days later to the professor and I said, it doesn't work, right?
zh: 于是两天后我回到教授那里,我说,这东西不管用,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I started an argument with my professor at Stanford.
zh: 然后我就和我在斯坦福的教授吵起来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it was like, what, the next two class periods were just me and the professor arguing over why his design didn't work.
zh: 你知道吗,接下来的两个课时就是我和教授在争论为什么他的设计不工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had a book that was being published with that design in it.
zh: 他有一本书正在出版,里面收录了那个设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was very annoying.
zh: 这让他非常恼火。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, it was very time-sensitive for him.
zh: 哦,对他来说时间上非常紧迫。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we started built-in self-test, right?
zh: 然后我们开始做内建自测试(built-in self-test),对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember Ed McCluskey at Stanford was my professor, and he was sort of the father of that.
zh: 我记得斯坦福的 Ed McCluskey 是我的教授,他算是那个领域的鼻祖。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had wonderful arguments around why most of his ideas were bad.
zh: 我们有过非常精彩的争论,争论为什么他的大部分想法都不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: They weren't practical for real chips, but I was putting built-in self-test to work on the three and six.
zh: 那些想法对真实芯片来说不实用,但我正在把内建自测试用在那三和六上。

speaker: Unknown
en: John Hennessy was my thesis advisor, and obviously he did okay.
zh: John Hennessy 是我的论文导师,显然他后来混得不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: I helped his career, he became president, and he's not okay since then.
zh: 我帮了他的事业,他当上了校长,从那以后他就“不”错了(he's not okay)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是啊,是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Later on, we'll talk about the CIS courses, this kind of debate.
zh: 稍后我们会谈谈 CIS 课程,这种争论。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had the same experience when I was teaching at Stanford.
zh: 我在斯坦福教书时也有过同样的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: You come with something that you think is the truth, and then the student comes that works in industries, well, actually, not quite.
zh: 你带着一个自己认为是真理的东西来,然后一个在工业界工作的学生来了,说,嗯,其实不是那么回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the next lecture you come back with, okay, I looked this up, you're right, this is outdated.
zh: 于是下一堂课你回来说,好吧,我查了一下,你是对的,这个已经过时了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and I'll tell you, you know, that's part of the, you know, that interaction, and I think that's part of what makes Silicon Valley so unique.
zh: 是啊,我告诉你,你知道,这种互动,我觉得这正是让硅谷如此独特的一部分原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right, you know, is you have so many companies and entrepreneurship, it's like in the water here, right?
zh: 对,你知道,就是这里有这么多公司和创业精神,创业就像融在空气里一样,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Starting things up and new ideas and challenging the professors, and you can't be a professor at a place like Stanford and not expect to get challenged and enjoy it.
zh: 开创事业、新想法、挑战教授——你在斯坦福这样的地方当教授,就不能不预期被挑战,而且要乐在其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a good foot traffic in and out of that ivory tower.
zh: 那座象牙塔进进出出的人流量很可观。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, no, 486 was your big... Yeah.
zh: 是啊,对,486 是你的大……是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Accomplishment, if you will.
zh: 成就,可以这么说。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, lots of people worked on it.
zh: 显然有很多人参与了这项工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you guys broke some new ground in chip design there, right?
zh: 而且你们在芯片设计上开辟了一些新领域,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And increased what functions the chip was supposed to do and so on and so forth.
zh: 还增加了芯片本该实现的功能,等等诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it was a pretty magic period as well because it was before what you would think of as the EDA industry.
zh: 是的,那也是一段非常神奇的时期,因为它是在你通常所说的 EDA 产业出现之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh wow, yes, that's right.
zh: 哦哇,是的,没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the end of the, a little bit of the 386, but the 486 was really the first chip to implement what you would think of as modern EDA techniques.
zh: 在那之后,386 稍微有一点,但 486 才是真正第一个实现你通常所说的现代 EDA 技术的芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did a high-level design, right, a description, an RTL description, but there was no Verilog.
zh: 我们做了高层设计,对吧,一个描述,一个 RTL 描述,但当时没有 Verilog。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we invented HDL, right?
zh: 所以我们发明了 HDL,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: The Intel hardware description language.
zh: Intel 硬件描述语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I wrote my own language.
zh: 所以我自己写了一门语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you had to build a compiler for that language, right?
zh: 嗯,那你就得为那门语言造一个编译器,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So we created a compiler for the language.
zh: 所以我们为那门语言做了个编译器。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was no automatic placing route.
zh: 当时没有自动布局布线。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we had to invent that.
zh: 所以我们得把它发明出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we worked with Alberto Sanjivangi, Vincentelli, Berkeley, and some of his students for the first, you know, placement, the first routing, the first automated timing management.
zh: 然后我们和伯克利的 Alberto Sanjivangi、Vincentelli 以及他的一些学生合作,做出了第一个布局、第一个布线、第一个自动化的时序管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they created EDATA into something.
zh: 所以他们把 EDATA 创造成了某种东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, to a great degree that, you know, and that was really one of the hallmarks that not only was the 486 this compatible pipeline microprocessor, but we ushered in many of the foundations of what became the modern EDA industry and was really a pretty magical period of the industry.
zh: 是的，在很大程度上是这样，你知道，那确实是其中的一个标志，不仅 486 是兼容流水线的微处理器，而且我们开创了后来成为现代 EDA 产业基础的诸多东西，那确实是这个行业相当神奇的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是啊，是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we look at today, will people look back as Blackwell and saying this was of the last generation that was done before AI took over the design process for Microsoft?
zh: 如果我们看今天，人们回望 Blackwell 时，会不会说这是 AI 接管 Microsoft 设计流程之前的最后一代产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we in a similar transition right now?
zh: 我们现在是否正处于一个类似的转型之中？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are certainly aspects of that.
zh: 我认为确实有这方面的因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think when you look at things like Jalapeno today, right, you sort of say that's sort of a first principles use of AI.
zh: 而且我认为，当你今天看像 Jalapeno 这样的东西时，对吧，你会说那算是一种第一性原理式的 AI 应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the chip design process, right, where you throw out a lot of those things.
zh: 在芯片设计流程中，对吧，你会把很多那些东西都抛掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, there are pieces of design that are still really hard, right, in that sense.
zh: 当然，设计中有一些部分仍然非常难，对吧，从这个意义上说。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of the analog, right, aspects, certes is probably the best example of that, you know, are still not AI-able, right?
zh: 我们理解如何把它组合成正确的乘加寄存器结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just need lots of silicon data, right, to get those.
zh: 你就是需要大量的硅片数据，对吧，才能搞定那些。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you either get so conservative in your analog design that you're able to, I'll say, AI it, or, right, you got to do those the hard way.
zh: 所以你要么把模拟设计做得非常保守，以至于能够，我这么说吧，用 AI 来做，要么，对吧，你就得用笨办法去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now many of the logic functions can really be done with AI tools and techniques in pretty incredible ways, right?
zh: 但现在许多逻辑功能确实可以用 AI 工具和技术以相当惊人的方式完成，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Your transistor budgets are big enough.
zh: 你的晶体管预算已经足够大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The design tools are getting smart enough.
zh: 设计工具也变得足够聪明了。

speaker: Unknown
en: A few experts guiding the tools and how to apply it.
zh: 再加上少数专家指导工具以及如何应用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I really think it will be somewhat like the 46 that way, right?
zh: 而且我真的认为它会有些像 46 那样，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We just sort of look back and say, yep, that was the beginning of a new era of chip design.
zh: 我们回望时只会说，是的，那是芯片设计新时代的开端。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whenever you have the technology to make something easy, that means the bottleneck moves somewhere else.
zh: 每当你拥有让某件事变容易的技术，就意味着瓶颈移动到了别处。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we guess at this point where the bottleneck will be in the future?
zh: 在这个时点，我们能猜到未来的瓶颈会在哪里吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some things which it seems like AI is incredibly good at, right?
zh: 有一些事情似乎 AI 极其擅长，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like creating the software layers, you know, writing kernels, a lot of the
zh: 比如创建软件层，你知道，编写内核，很多……

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of this sort of being able to specify the objectives at a higher level, which then gets sort of translated into Verilog, right?
zh: 我认为很多这类事情，比如能够在更高的层次上指定目标，然后被转换成 Verilog，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what is the new frontier?
zh: 那么新的前沿在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the thing that will be difficult going forward?
zh: 接下来会困难的事情是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, when you look at today, so let's say Guido and Pat, we're off to do a great new chip together.
zh: 嗯，你看今天，比方说 Guido 和 Pat，我们打算一起做一款很棒的新芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to, right, right.
zh: 我们要做，对，对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's the one that's going to leap ahead because we have understanding of the AI.
zh: 而且它会领先一大截，因为我们理解 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have understanding of the AI workloads.
zh: 我们理解 AI 工作负载。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have understanding then of how to compose that into the right multiply, accumulate, register structure.
zh: 那么我们就理解了如何把它组合成正确的乘法、累加、寄存器结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: Perfect visibility of the model workloads of tomorrow as well.
